reader.requirement: At --std 85, FUNCTION LOG10 ( argument-1 ) must be accepted with exactly one numeric argument (item, signed literal, expression) and refused with two (comma- or space-separated), zero, an empty '( )', or no list; a floating-point literal argument (a 2002 introduction) must be refused at 85.

edition-consulted.switches: the D8 edition window: IntrinsicSig.IntroducedIn (85 for the 1989 module rows) against ctx.Edition.DialectLevel, COBOL1502/COBOL1503
Constructs.FunctionEmptyArgumentList2002: an empty '( )' argument list is COBOL0900 below 2002
Constructs.FloatingPointLiteral2002: a floating-point numeric literal is COBOL0900 below 2002

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 an empty '( )' list and a floating-point literal argument are refused by COBOL0900 (2002 introductions); the one-argument arity is the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: l1-log10-two-arguments covers the two-argument refusal (COBOL1504); the accepted forms, the zero/empty/no-list refusals and the float-literal edition arm are not exercised

probes.printed: COBOL1504 LOG10 takes 1 argument(s); 2 given (10, 10) / 0 given ('()' and no list); COBOL0900 an empty function argument list requires COBOL-2002; COBOL0900 a floating-point numeric literal requires COBOL-2002 for LOG10(1.0E2)
probes.expected: refuse each: the format admits exactly one argument; 1.0E2 is not a 1985 literal

reader.notes: The format quotation ('FUNCTION LOG10 ( argument-1 )') is below cite.py's four-word floor; clause A.2.21.2 was read directly in specs/ANSI_COBOL_1985.md. Arity comes from the catalog row LOG10 Fixed 1..1, IntroducedIn 85, and the edition-gated literal and empty-list forms are refused at 85.

refuter.evidence: rfmt1.cob: LOG10(H - 900) -> 2; LOG10(FUNCTION LOG10(H) + 7) -> 1; 'LOG10 (H)' -> 3; LOG10(H ** 2) -> 6. rfmt2.cob: LOG10(H -1) two arguments COBOL1504; LOG10(H; H) COBOL1504; LOG10(H)(1:2) COBOL1629. rfmt3/rfmt4 (class c): no FUNCTION keyword or REPOSITORY form at 85 refused. rfmt5.cob: LOG10(.000000000000000001) -> -18; LOG10(999999999999999999) prints 018.000000000000 where the true value truncated to 12 places is 017.999999999999: an approximation, which §1989:A.2.21.4 RV1 permits (OK 'approximation of the logarithm to the base 10'), and a returned-value matter outside this format rule. cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.3.3 SR1/SR2.
